## Procedure

- Run `git fetch origin` and `git log origin/main --oneline --grep "Remudero-Task: <base id>$" -1` to confirm the base merged.
- Run `git log --format="%h %s%n%b" origin/main..HEAD` and list this task's own commits. Leave out every commit with another task's `Remudero-Task` trailer and every plan commit whose files now match main.
- Run `git worktree add <dir> -b run-W1-T<n>-<new ms> origin/main` for a fresh branch. Keep the old branch.
- Run `git cherry-pick <each own commit>` in order, and resolve each conflict against main's merged version of the base.
- Run `git merge --no-edit origin/main` when main moved again. Keep git's own merge message: commitlint refuses a custom one.
- Run the task's own tests and its covering tests again with `node --test --import tsx --import ./test/setup/tmp-hygiene.ts <file>`: the merged base can change a contract the build reads (W1-T12414).
- Run `node --import tsx scripts/census-precheck.mjs --base origin/main` after the commit and confirm `census-precheck: OK`: main may have used the headroom (W1-T12416, ledgerHelperNames 52 > 51).
- Run `shipbuilt.sh <n>` with the new branch name in `~/rmd-work/ship/T<n>.branch`.

Boundaries: re-cut only an unpushed branch; a pushed one needs a new PR. The worker-branch-shape step refuses a branch that carries another task's trailer. No force-push.

## Evidence

- Azure ship logs: 12 histories mention a re-cut; 8 "re-cut tested; running PREP_ONLY shipbuilt.sh" lines.
- Mac ship logs: 8 re-cut mentions.
- shipbuilt.sh rebuilds a branch from main when its plan commit squash-merged.
